doc: Doc 5 · The Direction Governor · Northena · M10

rules.docx_rule_text_verbatim: A5.1 · Deterministic by construction, enforced structurally [CANON]. No Northena module imports a machine-learning library or a learned component, and an import assertion enforcing this runs in continuous integration. Determinism is checked structurally, not by review. The moment a direction governor adjusts gating from past runs, or infers scope probabilistically, it stops being auditable — and auditability is its entire reason to exist.

A5.2 · The accountability standard [CANON]. Every run must be answerable deterministically: admitted because these fields were valid; gated in because scope membership held; stopped because this condition was met; refused because this rule fired. "Admitted because the model scored it highly enough" is the unauditable outcome this standard exists to prevent.

rules.statement_short: Admit freezes; judgement is borrowed, never performed
rules.docx_rule_text_verbatim: A5.3 · Admit freezes; judgement is borrowed, never performed [CANON]. Admit compiles, validates, and freezes. Where compilation genuinely needs judgement — resolving an ambiguous scope, setting a preservation depth or a floor — Admit invokes the depth governor (Solva, Document 4) through an opaque handle and freezes the value it returns. The judgement is the reasoner's; the freeze is Northena's alone. Northena never reads that governor's internals and never performs inference itself.

rules.statement_short: Gate is strict set-membership, with no inferential path
rules.docx_rule_text_verbatim: A5.4 · Gate is strict set-membership, with no inferential path [CANON]. Gate tests whether a sub-objective falls within the scope the frozen artifact declares — membership against a defined set, and nothing else. Ambiguous membership is a compilation defect resolved at Admit by the reasoner, never a Gate-time judgement. No inferential path exists in Gate. This is the specific mechanism by which a massive context cannot pull the run off-objective: scope is a frozen set, and adjacency is not membership.

rules.statement_short: Converge owns the halt on fixed conditions
rules.docx_rule_text_verbatim: A5.5 · Converge owns the halt on fixed conditions [CANON]. Converge decides termination on two conditions fixed in the frozen artifact, both threshold checks: done-condition met terminates as success; budget exhausted terminates on budget; neither continues. There is no learned stopping. The depth governor may report it cannot reason further soundly — that report is an input Converge acts on, but the stop decision and its record belong to Northena alone, because a component that could stop a run without Northena recording why would put a termination outside the audit surface entirely.

rules.statement_short: The budget is a hard stop
rules.docx_rule_text_verbatim: A5.6 · The budget is a hard stop [CANON]. A run halts at its ceiling and nothing past it is billed. This is what makes an open-ended run commissionable at all: exposure is bounded at commit, by a number the commissioner set, enforced by the governor rather than by the executor that could be tempted to keep going.

rules.statement_short: The freeze is atomic; the artifact is immutable for the run
rules.docx_rule_text_verbatim: B5.1 · The freeze is atomic; the artifact is immutable for the run [CANON]. A changed intent is a new admission, never an edit of a live one. The frozen artifact carries type and identity, version, scope set, defensibility floor, done-condition, budget, and lawful basis.

rules.statement_short: Lawful basis is enforced at Admit, before any extraction
rules.docx_rule_text_verbatim: B5.2 · Lawful basis is enforced at Admit, before any extraction [CANON]. Purpose limitation is an admission property, not a downstream filter — a run with no lawful basis never starts, so no material is ever touched under an unstated basis. Five deterministic validity checks run in order at Admit, each with its own refusal reason; a failure at any point refuses the admission and writes the reason, and no downstream stage runs.

rules.statement_short: Two admission paths, both freezing the same way
rules.docx_rule_text_verbatim: B5.3 · Two admission paths, both freezing the same way [CANON]. An external request is checked and frozen at Admit having arrived complete; a work order cannot freeze until the shaping conversation completes the objective envelope — the shaping dialogue is where the envelope is filled, Admit is where it is checked and frozen. Both paths write a Ledger row carrying the artifact reference and the lawful-basis reference. (The shaping dialogue for commissioning work — including training work — is specified in Document 12; its output is an envelope Admit freezes.)

rules.statement_short: The Ledger writer exposes append only
rules.docx_rule_text_verbatim: B5.4 · The Ledger writer exposes append only [CANON]. No update path and no delete path exists within the retention window. A correction is a new entry referencing what it corrects. This is enforced as code: the ledger writer exposes append and nothing else, checked by import assertion. Out-of-scope and refused items are recorded, never silently dropped.

rules.statement_short: The stamp-audit side-channel is deliberately permissive
rules.docx_rule_text_verbatim: B5.5 · The stamp-audit side-channel is deliberately permissive [CANON]. The Ledger absorbs untyped side-channel entries from other engines — boundary emissions, measurement stamps, trace correlation, gate receipts, refusal envelopes — without mutating the frozen row contract. Typing it would harden it into a mutation surface; the permissiveness is guarded by a snapshot test so the decision cannot be quietly reversed. Unit and audit stay in separate envelopes with separate lifecycles, joined by identity rather than embedded.
